# Agents, tools and protocols

English · [Русский](../ru/themes/agents-tools.md) · ← [AI Interview Atlas](../../README.md)

Agent loops, tool design, memory, termination, human approval and protocols such as MCP.

## Both tracks

- **When does splitting work among agents improve results, and when do coordination costs dominate?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether task independence and shared-state conflicts guide orchestration.
- **How would you make an agent's production actions reversible where possible and auditable where reversal is impossible?**
  - System design · Asked at: [Palantir](../companies/palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether compensating actions and durable evidence are planned before execution.
- **Design human approval for consequential agent actions, including how approval remains bound to the exact action being executed.**
  - System design · Asked at: [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) †, [Palantir](../companies/palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether approval controls are enforced outside the model.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Preview the concrete action, target and consequences before approval.
    - Bind approval to validated arguments and recheck authorisation at execution.
    - Record the decision and execution result; expire approval after material changes.
  - Read: [Building Effective AI Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents) (Anthropic) · [Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency](https://stripe.com/blog/idempotency) (Stripe)
- **Design an agent that creates and updates work orders in a live ERP without duplicating or silently corrupting business operations.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Palantir](../companies/palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether business invariants survive uncertain model and network behaviour.

## AI Engineering

- **What does interleaving reasoning with tool observations add to a language-model agent compared with reasoning alone?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether external feedback changes the agent's next action.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Distinguish a planned action from an observation returned by the environment.
    - Use observations to update the next step and detect failed assumptions.
    - Discuss tool failures and the extra latency of repeated interaction.
  - Read: [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629) (Yao et al., arXiv)
- **Design recovery from tool errors and timeouts, including cases where a timed-out call may already have changed external state.**
  - System design · Asked at: [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) †
  - Tests: Whether retries preserve correctness as well as availability.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Classify transient, permanent and ambiguous outcomes before retrying.
    - Use idempotency keys or reconcile external state after uncertain writes.
    - Bound attempts and deadlines; add backoff, jitter and an escalation path.
  - Read: [Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency](https://stripe.com/blog/idempotency) (Stripe)
- **How do schema-constrained responses differ from function calls, and which component actually executes an action?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether valid syntax is distinguished from authorised execution.
- **What does MCP standardise between an AI application and an external service that a model's function-call format does not?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Microsoft](../companies/microsoft.md) †
  - Tests: Whether protocol transport and capabilities are separated from model decisions.
- **How would you select, name and document tools so that a model chooses the right operation and arguments?**
  - System design · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †
  - Tests: Whether tool design reduces ambiguity and measurable misuse.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Expose cohesive operations with unambiguous names and validated schemas.
    - Return relevant, bounded results and actionable error messages.
    - Evaluate tool selection and arguments on realistic tasks, then remove confusing overlap.
  - Read: [Writing effective tools for AI agents—using AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents) (Anthropic)
- **Design memory for an agent that works across many sessions: what is persisted, retrieved, revised and forgotten?**
  - System design · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †
  - Tests: Whether durable state is distinguished from transient context.
- **How should an agent decide whether to answer directly or obtain fresh information with a tool?**
  - Knowledge
  - Tests: Whether uncertainty, freshness and tool cost influence the decision.
- **Define completion and stopping conditions for an agent loop so it cannot spend indefinitely on an unfinished task.**
  - System design
  - Tests: Whether progress, budgets and terminal states are explicit.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Separate success, blocked, cancelled and budget-exhausted outcomes.
    - Track progress using observable state, with step, cost and time limits.
    - Checkpoint enough state to resume or hand off without repeating side effects.
  - Read: [Building Effective AI Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents) (Anthropic)
- **A long-running agent confidently pursues the wrong objective. How do you locate where its task state diverged and recover?**
  - Applied scenario
  - Tests: Whether diagnosis uses task state and observations rather than confidence in prose.
- **For a coding agent, how would you separate the model's contribution from the harness's contribution to reliable task completion?**
  - System design · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †
  - Tests: Whether controlled comparisons can identify the source of improvements.
- **Why might an enterprise agent operate on an ontology of business objects and actions instead of raw tables and documents?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Palantir](../companies/palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether semantic modelling is connected to valid operations and permissions.
